source.title: Compendio básico de la gramática ralámuli
source.publication_context: Gobierno del Estado de Chihuahua / Coordinación Estatal de la Tarahumara

source_general_analysis.color_roots: The source states that color words use the ending -ame, labeled participio, and that color roots normally occur with one or more endings.

intensity_material.-ka/-ga/-cha: described in the source as related to stronger/intensified color
intensity_material.-simi: becoming/inchoative motion-like expression in color constructions

source_general_analysis.important_scope: Descriptions are source-level labels from the Compendio; this project does not automatically equate their morphemic status across every variety.

forms.source_note: source explicitly notes absence of siyókame in this variety

basic_color_paradigms.source_semantic_note: Norte, Baja and Baja-TB distinguish rosákame 'white' from rosáname 'medium/light white'; Cumbre is reported not to maintain the same distinction consistently.

additional_color_evidence.significance: documents both bare -ame/-ami and forms with additional material before -me
independent bare -ame/-ami alternation in the color domain
shows -ami/-me embedded in more complex color derivations

analytical_findings.me_mi_m_variation: The same semantic color categories exhibit final -me, -mi and contracted -m across varieties.
analytical_findings.ka_na_variation: The material immediately before -me/-mi varies between -ka and -na according to color, degree/state and variety.
analytical_findings.bare_ame_ami: Some color terms occur with -ame/-ami without the -ka/-na material visible in the basic red/black/white paradigms.
analytical_findings.independence_value: This source provides synchronically distributed evidence across multiple Rarámuri varieties and is methodologically independent of the unresolved SRC-02/Hilton document lineage.
analytical_findings.diachronic_value: The source strongly supports treating -ame/-ami as a recurrent derivational/participial core while analyzing additional k/n/g material separately rather than assuming one linear surface change -ameke > -ami.

comparison_constraints: Do not equate historical Steffel -ame-ke with modern -ka-me merely because both contain k and ame-like material; published analyses place the material in different orders.
Do not assume final -e/-i alternation is a single sound law without variety-specific phonological evidence.
Do not assume contracted -m has the same pathway in all varieties without prosodic analysis.
Human verification against page images is required before publication-quality transcription of every diacritic and regional label.
